answer: Submissions that land within 224 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The bridge detector writes to cipher, and quartz shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 222 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 14 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
